I've never read any literature about it, but if you replaced the current tax structure with high rates of tax on land it would probably put a lot of farmers out of business and all you would be left with are the huge corporate farms. Do you think that just having a tax on land would be a good idea?

This is generally called "Georgism", after Henry George who popularized it in the United States. If you look up "Georgism" on the Internet, you will find out the big problem with this idea right now - the basic idea has been hijacked by a way-radical group of environmentalists who conceive of a single land tax as a way to tax human existence to the breaking point in order to reduce the number of humans. These same people also don't mind ginning up class politics between landlords and tenants, which a tax on land ownership also accomplishes efficiently.

The biggest problem with a single land tax, though is that it makes land ownership a privilege granted by the state, rather than a right, and would therefore allow the government to withdraw anyone's right to own land simply by asserting that they hadn't paid the land tax -or that they hadn't paid enough, or that the government was not obliged to accept the land tax payment, or that the government had an obligation to manage the number of property owners for maximum economic efficiency, or whatever. They could accomplish a Kelo taking any time they wanted to, with all that implies.

Now, any tax has consequences that reduce one's rights, some more, some less, and there's no way to avoid it. But a single land tax is no good - unfortunately. The economic principles that the idea comes from are sound, but the real consequences would be terrible.

any tax has consequences that reduce one's rights, some more, some less, and there's no way to avoid it.

How does not taxing one at all reduce one's rights?

You can say "there's no sane way to avoid I", if you must. The problem with no taxes is no police and no courts, so no real property rights at all - someone can just come take your stuff. That reduces your rights to zero.

What gives you the idea that you have the authority to forcibly take money from people just because they live on land?

Presumably you also favor a sea and air tax as well to prevent people from moving to these tax havens?
Thomas Paine's Agrarian Justice may be of interest to you.

Thomas Paine was a great rabble-rouser, but he was no economist. His ideas were formed in the context of the American colonies having huge amounts of unclaimed, unimproved frontier land, overbalancing the land under development. There's nowhere left like that.

By Default, All Muslims are obliged to fast all of Ramadan. However, there are several conditions that render one incapable of fasting as it might effect one's health or safety. Medicine to be taken throughout the day is an example of an obligatory commitment that most of the times cannot be postponed until after iftar. What's the deal then?

Fasting is a must for every sane, mature, and healthy individual. Muslims that have not hit puberty are not required to fast, however encouraged to adjust to it for later on.

As stated over and over in the holy Qur'an, Allah does not force anyone to do a certain act that they are not capable of - no matter what it is. As a result, one may be excused from fasting.

Below are conditions and life situations that allow the Muslim to break the fast.

Traveling

Almighty Allah says,

"… The month of Ramadhan [is that] in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for the people and clear proofs of guidance and criterion. So whoever sights [the new moon of] the month, let him fast it; and whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days. Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship and [wants] for you to complete the period and to glorify Allah for that [to] which He has guided you; and perhaps you will be grateful.." - [Al-Baqarah: 185]

God has licensed every muslim that is traveling to break the fast, as long as they aren't traveling for the sole purpose of avoiding fasting. The Minimal traveling distance set for this license to be valid is 85 km (53 miles). Moreover, these days that the muslim has abstained from fasting due to traveling are not forgotten, but are to be fasted later on.

Illness & Old Age

Almighty Allah says,

“... The month of Ramadhan [is that] in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for the people and clear proofs of guidance and criterion. So whoever sights [the new moon of] the month, let him fast it; and whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days. Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship and [wants] for you to complete the period and to glorify Allah for that [to] which He has guided you; and perhaps you will be grateful.” - [al-Baqarah:185]

If one is temporary ill during ramadan, then the travelling license applies here as well and they are to repeat the missed days later on.

Almighty Allah says,

“... [Fasting for] a limited number of days. So whoever among you is ill or on a journey [during them] - then an equal number of days [are to be made up]. And upon those who are able [to fast, but with hardship] - a ransom [as substitute] of feeding a poor person [each day]. And whoever volunteers excess - it is better for him. But to fast is best for you, if you only knew.” - [al-Baqarah:184]

If one is permanently ill with no hopes of recovery, or too old to fast causing difficulty then they are exempt from fasting. At this point, one can either:

  • Fast
  • Feed one poor person for every day you do not fast

Menstruating & Post-natal bleeding

If a woman is menstruating or is in post-natal bleeding stage, then she is obliged to abstain from fasting and repeat the fasting of the missing days later on.

Pregnancy & Breast feeding

Pregnant and breast feeding women and their offsprings may be affected with weak health if they are to commit to fasting. Hence, it is halal/permissible for them to abstain from fasting and repeat the missing days later on.
